patch_description:
The current program (Gen 10) scores 0.46 with 7 distinct parameters and shows weaker worst-group margin (0.25) and validation margin (0.43) compared to Gen 9 (score 0.54, worst-group margin 0.31, validation margin 0.58). The key issue is insufficient parameter count and entanglement diversity.

The prior Gen 9 program achieved score 0.54 with 12 distinct parameters using fine-grained control over diagonal ZZ couplings: `"zz_03"` and `"zz_47"` on separate diagonals. The current Gen 10 collapsed this to one shared `"diag"` parameter on only [0,4] and [2,6], losing expressive power.

The recommendation: split the shared `"diag"` ZZ parameter into two independent parameters—`"zz_04"` for wires [0,4] and `"zz_26"` for wires [2,6]—boosting the distinct parameter count from 7 to 9. This minimal 2-parameter increase restores finer control over long-range entanglement while maintaining shallow depth and preserving the proven near-neighbor + cross-layer + diagonal architecture. The tighter coupling between the two halves of the qubit space should improve worst-group margin separation and reduce the generalization gap.

Additional refinement: add one more ZZ gate on the complementary diagonal pair [1,5] with parameter `"zz_15"` to achieve symmetric full diagonal coverage, bringing the total to 10 distinct parameters. This maintains parameter economy while improving expressiveness and should yield validation margins closer to 0.58 and worst-group margin closer to 0.31.
